title: Growth Analytics Manager
description:
Role Purpose Haleon Indias e-commerce business is a priority growth lever, and the Growth Analytics Manager is the person who turns our platform and market data into decisions. The role owns the business intelligence layer for DCommerce: platform-level dashboards, city-level reporting and daily market share tracking across marketplaces, quick commerce and e-pharma for all brands. This is not a reporting/ data analytics role. The Growth Analytics Manager defines what we measure, makes sure the numbers can be trusted, and tells the business what to do next. What Will The Person Own Platform dashboards: one consistent, decision-ready dashboard view per platform (offtake units, MRP value, NSV, share, availability, pricing), with brand, subcategory, SKU and NPI cuts built in. City-level reporting: city and cluster views of QCom and marketplace performance, so we can see where we are winning or losing, not just how we are doing nationally; and actionability on pincodes/ RPI with strongly correlated inputs of promos and visibility Daily market share view: brand and subcategory share, built from platform external analytics, tracked daily with clear trend and exception flags. Metric definitions and data trust: the single set of KPI definitions for DCom (including multipack and virtual combo treatment, and platform-specific quirks such as Amazon Core, Fresh and Now), and sign-off on every dashboard before it reaches leadership. Key Responsibilities Business Intelligence: Design, platform dashboards in Power BI (or equivalent) on top of the clean data layer provided by the Data Analyst; own the business logic, visuals and usability. Build the analytics reporting module within the existing DCom dashboard: platform views, NPI tracking shown separately from base business, multipack and combo views. Maintain a dashboard release and QC checklist so that numbers reconcile across offtake, MRP, NSV and platform-reported views. City-Level Market Share Intelligence: Build city-level views of share, offtake, availability and pricing, using the city and pincode mapping on external data. Identify under-indexed cities and clusters by brand and platform, and convert them into specific actions (assortment, availability, visibility, activation). Track daily share movements at brand and subcategory level; flag material shifts, competitor moves and root causes within the same week. Insight to Action: Run weekly, monthly and quarterly performance reviews: what happened, why, and what we should do about it, with owners and follow-up on actions. Deliver brand and platform deep dives that lead to a decision (for example share erosion in a subcategory, OOS impact on a hero SKU, or a pricing gap versus competition). Partner with Digital Shelf to bring shopper research into the business narrative, so reviews combine the numbers with the shopper reasons behind them. Promo, Pricing Growth Analytics: Own promo effectiveness analytics for e-commerce: uplift, ROI and cannibalisation by platform and brand. Manage the promo planning file and its platform-wise splits, so one master plan is adapted and shared correctly with each platform. Planning Strategy Support: Support the annual and quarterly planning cycle with baselines, scenario models and growth lever sizing by brand, platform and city tier. Contribute to channel mix and competitor benchmarking so strategy is anchored on external facts as well as our own data. Skillsets Must have 3-6 years in business analysis, e-commerce analytics, category management or BI, ideally in FMCG or consumer health. Strong Power BI (or Tableau) skills: you have built dashboards end to end, including data modelling and DAX or equivalent, not just consumed them. Advanced Excel (Power Query, complex modelling) and working SQL; Python is a plus. Sound understanding of Indian e-commerce and quick commerce: how offtake, share, availability and pricing behave across platforms. A structured storytelling habit: you move from what happened, to why, to what we should do, and you can defend the number in the room. Comfortable questioning data: you spot anomalies and push back on numbers that do not reconcile. Good to have Experience with digital shelf or market share tools such as Gobblecube, NIQ, Profitero or similar. Exposure to promo analytics, pricing or RGM-style analysis. City or geo-level analysis experience (pincode, dark store or cluster mapping). Prior experience supporting annual planning or QBR cycles.

title: Analyst-Data Analytics (Agentic)
description:
The Analytics, Investment Optimization and Marketing Enablement (AIM) team - a part of Global Commercial Services Marketing group within American Express - is the analytical engine that enables the Global Commercial Card & Non-Card business. The team enables profitable business growth through data, analytics, decision science and AI-powered capabilities, providing actionable insights and innovative solutions to drive business and marketing strategy. This role, based out of Gurugram, will be a part of the AIM team and will focus on developing and applying advanced Data Science and Generative AI solutions across Global Commercial Services. The incumbent will work on high-impact business problems spanning customer acquisition, engagement, targeting and personalization, product and portfolio analytics, marketing measurement and analytical productivity. The role will focus on applying Generative AI to business and analytical problems and translating opportunities into hands-on solutions and prototypes. The incumbent will apply Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), prompt engineering, agentic AI and other emerging AI techniques alongside traditional Data Science and Machine Learning approaches. The position is part of a highly collaborative environment, working with partners across AIM, GCS Marketing, Product, Capabilities, Technology and other teams at American Express. Qualifications Bachelor s or Master s degree in a quantitative or technical field such as Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence or a related discipline. 0-3 years of relevant experience in Data Science, Machine Learning, Generative AI or Analytics, with demonstrated hands-on experience developing Generative AI solutions through professional work, internships, academic research or substantial projects. Strong programming skills in Python and working knowledge of SQL, with the ability to manipulate data, conduct analysis and develop Data Science/AI solutions. Strong foundation in Data Science and Machine Learning concepts, including statistical modeling, supervised and unsupervised learning, model evaluation and experimentation. Hands-on understanding of Large Language Models and core GenAI techniques such as prompt engineering and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), including concepts such as embeddings, semantic retrieval and using relevant data and context to improve LLM responses. Understanding of approaches for evaluating GenAI solutions across dimensions such as response quality, relevance, consistency and reliability. Strong analytical/conceptual thinking acumen with the ability to structure and solve unstructured and complex business problems. Ability and curiosity to rapidly learn, experiment with and apply emerging AI techniques to practical business problems. Excellent written and oral communication skills with the ability to articulate technical concepts and analytical findings clearly. Preferred Qualifications Hands-on exposure to agentic AI concepts and workflows involving capabilities such as tool use, reasoning or multi-step orchestration. Experience with GenAI/LLM frameworks and libraries such as LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Hugging Face or equivalent tools. Experience with vector-based retrieval, semantic search, advanced RAG techniques or LLM evaluation frameworks. Familiarity with commercial and open-source LLMs and considerations involved in selecting appropriate models and approaches for different use cases. Exposure to advanced GenAI techniques such as model fine-tuning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning or advanced retrieval approaches. Experience working with unstructured data or Natural Language Processing techniques. Familiarity with responsible AI principles and considerations related to applying AI within enterprise or regulated environments. Interest in applying AI and GenAI capabilities to marketing, customer engagement, personalization, analytical productivity and business decision-making. Develop hands-on Generative AI and Data Science solutions to solve complex and unstructured business problems across GCS. Design, build and experiment with LLM-powered solutions using techniques such as prompt engineering, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), embeddings, semantic search and vector-based retrieval. Develop and experiment with agentic AI workflows that can reason over context, leverage relevant data and tools, and support analytical and business decision-making. Develop and apply evaluation approaches for GenAI solutions across dimensions such as response quality, relevance, consistency and business effectiveness, with appropriate consideration for responsible AI, controls and governance. Apply Machine Learning and statistical techniques alongside Generative AI to develop fit-for-purpose solutions for customer acquisition, engagement, targeting, personalization, measurement and other business opportunities. Explore structured and unstructured data from multiple sources to identify relevant signals and develop innovative approaches that transform data into actionable insights and AI-powered solutions. Prototype, test and refine emerging GenAI techniques and collaborate with Technology, Capabilities and other partner teams, as appropriate, to support development of scalable solutions. Explore emerging LLMs, GenAI techniques and frameworks and assess their applicability to relevant GCS business and analytical problems. Work with business partners and other stakeholders to understand business needs, structure analytical problems and translate them into appropriate Data Science and GenAI approaches. Define appropriate analytical measures and success metrics, evaluate results and communicate findings, limitations and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Contribute to the development of reusable GenAI approaches, analytical assets and learnings that can support applications across AIM. Demonstrate curiosity and willingness to challenge the status quo; bring innovative thinking to generate insights, alternatives and opportunities for business success. Shift Time- 1:30 PM - 9:30 PM IST

description:
Job Overview We are seeking a seasoned, high-caliber logistics leader for the role of Director – Cross-Border Operations. Based out of our Gurgaon headquarters, you will lead end-to-end international logistics operations for Delhivery, overseeing cross-border import and export shipments across key global trade lanes. This is a strategic and execution-intensive role. You will spearhead the expansion of our international freight network by launching new country corridors and deferred air economy products, while driving revenue growth through strategic partnerships. This position owns P&L, SLA compliance, and operational efficiency for both air and ocean freight verticals. Key Responsibilities 1. End-to-End International Logistics Operations Lead end-to-end international logistics operations, managing and optimizing cross-border import and export shipments across global trade lanes. Supervise daily workflows for inbound and outbound cargo, ensuring smooth execution across origin handling, international linehaul, customs clearance, and last-mile delivery. Implement robust monitoring systems to track shipments, proactively resolve operational exceptions, and ensure high on-time delivery rates. Should be able to create and manage dashboards  Hold reviews internally with cross functional teams and externally with partners in destination country Should be able to design using BI tools and define metrics internally and for partners 2. Network Expansion & Product Development Spearhead the physical and operational expansion of Delhivery's international freight network by identifying and launching new country corridors. Design, launch, and scale deferred air economy products to offer competitive, cost-effective cross-border shipping options to e-commerce, SME, and enterprise clients. Establish standard operating procedures (SOPs) and operational readiness criteria for all newly launched corridors and lanes. 3. Strategic Partnerships & Carrier Management Identify, negotiate with, and onboard key global partners, including freight forwarders, customs house agents (CHAs), customs brokers, and commercial airlines/ocean carriers. Build and maintain strong strategic alliances to secure capacity commitments, preferential rate structures, and reliable transit times during peak and non-peak seasons. Manage partner performance SLAs, conducting regular reviews to ensure compliance with Delhivery's high operational standards. 4. P&L & SLA Compliance Management Take complete financial ownership of the Air and Ocean freight verticals, managing P&L, cost optimization, and overall unit economics (e.g., cost-per-kilogram and route margins). Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) such as Transit Turnaround Time (TAT), On-Time Delivery (OTD), Customs Clearance timelines, and first-contact dispute resolution. Control and minimize operational exceptions such as terminal storage costs, demurrage, detention fees, and flight offloads. 5. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Tech Enablement Collaborate closely with internal stakeholders including Sales, Business Development, Technology, and Legal/Compliance to support business growth and process standardization. Partner with Product and Engineering teams to build scalable, automated, and technology-driven processes for tracking, billing, and customs documentation. Ensure 100% adherence to international trade laws, customs regulations, aviation security standards, and safety compliances. Required Skills & Qualifications Experience & Education Education: Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, International Business, Engineering, or a related field. An MBA or Post-Graduate degree is highly preferred. Experience: 8+ years of progressive experience in international logistics, freight forwarding, or cross-border e-commerce shipping. Leadership: Minimum of 3+ years in a senior supervisory or managerial role directly overseeing air/ocean freight operations, partner management, or international linehaul. Core Competencies Domain Expertise: Deep working knowledge of air/ocean freight operations, global trade lanes, Incoterms 2020, customs clearance regulations, and HAWB/MAWB rules (aligned with our Global Air Freight Operations). Commercial & Financial Acumen: Strong experience managing P&L, negotiating complex commercial contracts, and optimizing unit economics. Analytical Rigor: Advanced proficiency in MS Excel and Google Sheets for tracking operations, data analysis, and building performance dashboards. Stakeholder & Vendor Management: Exceptional negotiation and relationship-building skills to manage high-level partnerships across multiple geographies. Problem-Solving: Strong critical-thinking and crisis-management abilities to handle transit disruptions, customs bottlenecks, and capacity constraints in a high-pressure environmen

title: AM-Taxation
description:
Job purpose: To support and independently manage day-to-day Direct Taxation and TDS compliances, including timely filing of TDS returns, reconciliation of books with statutory returns, preparation and response to Income Tax notices, tax data analysis, and coordination with internal teams and consultants. The role will also require a working understanding of GST and other indirect tax matters to support the overall Taxation function. 
 Primary responsibilities: 1. TDS Compliance & Return Filing • Ensure timely preparation and filing of quarterly TDS/TCS returns within statutory due dates. • Review TDS applicability and rates on various payments such as rent, professional fees, contractor payments, commission, interest and other business expenses. • Reconcile TDS deducted in books with TDS returns before filing. • Coordinate for correction/revised TDS returns wherever required. Monitor TDS challans, deductions, balances and statutory payment status. • Support issuance and reconciliation of Form 16/16A and other TDS certificates. 
 2. Books vs. Return Reconciliation Perform regular reconciliation between books of accounts and TDS returns. • Identify differences in TDS deduction, vendor PAN, amount, section, rate and challan details. • Reconcile TDS/TCS balances with Form 26AS/AIS/TIS, wherever applicable. Coordinate with Accounts, Payroll, Procurement and other departments for resolution of reconciliation differences. • Maintain proper reconciliation workings and supporting documents for audit and assessment purposes. 
 3. Income Tax Notices & Assessments • Monitor and maintain records of Income Tax notices, communications and proceedings. • Prepare data, reconciliations and supporting documents required for responding to Income Tax notices. • Coordinate with tax consultants and internal stakeholders for preparation and submission of replies. Assist in matters relating to TDS defaults, demands, assessments and other Income Tax proceedings. Track notice-wise status, due dates, submissions and closure of outstanding matters. Maintain a proper Income Tax Notice & Litigation Tracker. 
 4. Direct Tax Compliance & Taxation Support Assist in preparation of advance tax, self-assessment tax and tax computation workings. Support preparation of tax audit and income-tax-related schedules and information. Assist in computation and reconciliation of current tax and other direct tax-related balances. • Support statutory, internal and tax audits by providing required information and documents. • Keep track of amendments and notifications under the Income-tax Act, Rules and applicable TDS provisions. 
 5. GST / Indirect Tax Knowledge Possess working knowledge of GST provisions, GST returns and basic ITC concepts. Understand the interaction between GST and direct tax/TDS transactions wherever applicable. • Assist the Taxation Team in reconciliation and analysis of GST-related data when required. • Coordinate with the GST team for common tax data, vendor details and reconciliation requirements. Develop working knowledge of GST notices, compliance requirements and relevant provisions. 
 Required Skills: • Good knowledge of TDS/TCS provisions and Income-tax Act. • Practical experience in TDS return preparation and filing. • Strong reconciliation skills Books vs. TDS Returns vs. 26AS/AIS/TIS. • Experience in handling/preparing data for Income Tax notices and assessments. • Working knowledge of GST and indirect taxation. • Good knowledge of MS Excel, including Pivot Tables, XLOOKUP/VLOOKUP, SUMIFS and reconciliation techniques. • Good analytical and problem-solving skills. • Ability to coordinate with internal departments and external consultants

title: Sr. Manager - Aftersales Operations
description:
Badshahpur, Gurugram Full Time About Us Noise was built on a simple belief: India can build world-class consumer tech. Founded in 2014 by Amit Khatri and Gaurav Khatri, Noise began with a mission to democratize connected technology for every Indian. Today, we are Indias #1 smartwatch brand and #2 in TWS audio, with 40M+ users - and now backed by Bose as a strategic investor. Noises journey of innovation and impact has earned recognition both nationally and globally, with prestigious honours including the Economic Times Startup Award (2022), Forbes Leadership Awards (2023), Red Dot Design Award (2024), and Mobile India Awards (2025). The next phase is sharper: building a globally relevant, AI-native company where every function compounds leverage, not headcount. Join us as we continue to shape the sound of tomorrow! Your Will Bes We are looking for an experienced and hands-on Senior Manager - Aftersales Operations to own and drive the end-to-end Repair, Replacement, QC, Product Testing and Dispatch Operations across Audio, Wearables and other consumer electronics categories. The role will be responsible for ensuring that products received through customer returns, service centres, warehouses and other channels are accurately received, inspected, tested, repaired/replaced where applicable, dispositioned and dispatched within defined TATs, along with management of spares and inventory through the OMS platform. The individual will work closely with Customer Experience, Warehouse, Inventory, Logistics, Quality, Product, Technology and external service partners to ensure seamless execution of the aftersales lifecycle. This role requires a strong combination of operations management, technical understanding, QC expertise, inventory discipline, data analysis, process improvement and people leadership. 1. End-to-End Repair Replacement Operations Own the complete repair and replacement lifecycle from receipt of returned/defective products to final closure. Define and manage processes for product receiving, physical verification, serial number validation, QC inspection, functional testing, repair assessment, replacement approval, product disposition, inventory reconciliation and final dispatch through CRM. Establish clear SOPs and process controls to minimize leakage, delays, wrong replacements and incorrect dispositions. Ensure replacement products are dispatched within committed customer TAT. 2. Product QC Testing - Audio, Wearables Other Categories Own pre-dispatch and post-return QC/testing for Audio, Wearables and other consumer electronics categories. Define category-wise testing protocols and checklists for TWS/Earbuds, Headphones/Neckbands, Speakers/Audio products, Smartwatches/Smart Bands, Power Banks and other electronic accessories and NPD categories. Ensure complete functional testing before replacement dispatch, refurbishment, restocking, repair closure or customer shipment. Build testing parameters covering battery performance, charging, Bluetooth/pairing, audio output, microphone, touch/buttons, sensors, display, connectivity, app synchronization, physical condition, accessories and packaging. Ensure products failing QC are correctly segregated and do not enter saleable/replacement inventory. Continuously improve testing methodology based on emerging customer complaints and product defect trends. 3. Replacement Product Dispatch Management Own replacement dispatch readiness and ensure only QC-approved products are dispatched. Maintain controls around product model, SKU, serial number, colour/variant, product condition, accessories and packaging. Coordinate with Warehouse and Inventory teams to ensure replacement stock is available and accurately reflected in the system. Establish daily dispatch plans based on ageing and customer commitment. Track pending replacement cases and ensure there are no avoidable ageing cases. Identify bottlenecks causing delays in replacement dispatch and implement corrective actions. 4. TAT Management Own and monitor end-to-end aftersales TAT across receiving, QC, repair, replacement and dispatch. Define stage-wise TATs and SLAs for product receiving, QC inspection, technical testing, repair assessment, replacement approval, inventory allocation and dispatch. Maintain daily ageing dashboards and ensure cases crossing SLA are immediately escalated. Drive a culture of zero avoidable ageing within the team. Identify root causes of TAT breaches and implement preventive measures. Publish daily/weekly TAT performance reports to senior leadership. Key TAT Metrics tracked: Overall Repair TAT, Replacement TAT, QC TAT; Receiving-to-QC TAT, QC-to-Dispatch TAT; Average Ageing, Cases > SLA; First-Time-Right QC %, Dispatch SLA adherence %. 5. Returns Reverse Logistics Management Own the operational strategy for products returning from customers, service centres, marketplaces and other channels. Analyse return volumes and identify major drivers. Ensure returned products are correctly classified into Repairable, Replaceable, NTF/No Trouble Found, Physical Damage, Liquid Damage, Manufacturing Defect, Refurbishable, Scrap/Non-recoverable and Restockable. Ensure proper disposition and system closure of every returned unit. Work with Logistics and Warehouse teams to reduce reverse-logistics TAT and cost. 6. Root Cause Analysis Defect Reduction Analyse product return and QC data to identify recurring product and process failures. title: Business Analyst Finance, Risk & Fraud
description:
About the Role: 
 Hudson Data Private Limited is looking for a highly analytical Business Data Analyst with strong hands-on experience in SQL, data analysis, financial services, risk and/or fraud analytics. We are looking for candidates who can go beyond traditional requirement gathering and independently work with data to analyze input and output files, identify discrepancies, investigate anomalies, reconcile data, perform root-cause analysis, and translate findings into business and technical requirements. The ideal candidate should have experience working with complex datasets in Banking, FinTech, Lending, Payments, Risk, Fraud or Financial Services environments. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Analyze large datasets using SQL and Excel to identify trends, anomalies, exceptions and data-quality issues. Perform input vs. output analysis and validate data across multiple systems. Reconcile source data with system-generated outputs and identify missing, duplicate or incorrectly processed records. Perform root-cause analysis (RCA) for data discrepancies and system/process issues. Analyze financial transactions, customer/account data, risk indicators and fraud-related patterns. Understand business rules and validate whether system outputs are being generated correctly. Translate business problems into functional requirements, business rules, user stories and acceptance criteria. Work closely with Business, Product, Operations, Data and Technology teams. Create test scenarios and perform UAT and data validation. Use SQL to independently validate system changes and production results. Identify process gaps and recommend data-driven improvements and controls. Develop reports, dashboards and exception monitoring using Power BI/Tableau/QuickSight or similar tools. Clearly communicate analytical findings and recommendations to business and technical stakeholders. Must-Have Skills 6 to 10 years of relevant experience in Business Analysis / Data Analysis / Risk Analysis / Fraud Analysis. Strong hands-on SQL skills. Strong Excel skills, including PivotTables, XLOOKUP/VLOOKUP, SUMIFS/COUNTIFS and data reconciliation. Experience analyzing large datasets and input/output files. Strong experience in data reconciliation, exception analysis and root-cause analysis. Understanding of business rules and data-validation techniques. Experience with requirements gathering, user stories, acceptance criteria and UAT. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Good written and verbal communication skills. Preferred Skills Experience in Banking, FinTech, Lending, Payments, Credit Risk, Fraud or Financial Services. Experience analyzing financial or transactional data. Power BI / Tableau / QuickSight, Google Looker Basic Python knowledge. Understanding of APIs, JSON, databases, ETL and data pipelines. Jira / Confluence experience. Exposure to AWS / Azure / GCP is an advantage. What We Are Looking For We are looking for a candidate who can independently investigate: Input Data Business Rules Processing Output Exception Root Cause Resolution The candidate should be comfortable answering questions such as: Why does the output not match the input? Which records are impacted? What patterns exist in the exceptions? Is the issue caused by source data, mapping, transformation or business logic? How can SQL be used to validate the issue? What change is required? How should the solution be tested? This is not a purely documentation-based Business Analyst position. Strong hands-on data analysis and SQL capabilities are important for this role. 
 Preferred Candidate Background Candidates currently working as any of the following are encouraged to apply: Business Data Analyst | Business Analyst | Data Analyst | Risk Analyst | Fraud Analyst | Financial Data Analyst | Data Quality Analyst | Product Analyst Candidates with experience in FinTech, Banking, NBFC, Lending, Payments, Credit Risk, Fraud Detection, Transaction Monitoring, Reconciliation or Financial Data Analysis will be preferred. 
 Why Join Hudson Data? 
 At Hudson Data, youll be part of a dynamic, innovative, and globally connected team that combines advanced AI/ML frameworks, modern data technologies, and cloud-based analytics platforms to solve complex, real-world business challenges. Youll have the opportunity to experiment with new approaches, deepen your technical expertise, and see your work translate into measurable business impact within a culture that values creativity, precision, collaboration, and continuous learning. Our work spans high-impact domains including unsecured lending, BNPL, insurance, healthcare, and fraud analytics , where data science plays a critical role in solving commercially significant problems. Youll work on applications involving predictive modeling, risk scoring, fraud detection, customer and payment behavior, and decision intelligence providing the opportunity to apply advanced analytical techniques to problems where model quality directly influences business outcomes. For Data Scientists interested in applied machine learning rather than purely theoretical modeling , Hudson Data offers the opportunity to work at the intersection of advanced analytics, domain expertise, and real-world decision-making .

title: Assistant Manager, Business Insights
description:
The Assistant Manager - Business Insights will assist in leading and managing projects aimed at improving business processes and systems. This role involves working closely with different departments to analyze current processes, identify areas for improvement, and develop and implement solutions that enhance efficiency, quality, and customer satisfaction. 
 
 What You'll Do: 
 Opportunity identification on the ground: Continuously scan the operations to surface improvement avenues, inefficiencies, and performance gaps, and maintain a prioritized pipeline of opportunities backed by data and operational evidence. Problem framing: Partner with the account team and functional owners to convert vague asks and observed pain points into sharp, scoped problem statements with clear business impact and decision needs. Diagnostics & root-cause analysis: Run structured deep dives using data analysis, process walkthroughs, floor observation, segmentation, and Lean Six Sigma methods to move from symptoms to underlying drivers. Analysis & optimization: Build and maintain the analysis that drives decisions on the account - performance trends, driver analysis, and scenario comparisons - and translate findings into concrete optimization actions. Data & analytical quality: Validate data availability, definitions, and reliability; reconcile conflicting sources; document assumptions and limitations; and assure the accuracy and reproducibility of analytical outputs. Solution enablement & implementation support: Shape practical recommendations and support their implementation on the ground - coordinating owners, timelines, and dependencies so improvements are actually executed. Commercial & account insight: Connect findings to account economics - productivity, cost-to-serve, SLA/KPI exposure, quality, and client-impact implications. Technology & process enablement: Identify where recurring problems can be addressed through dashboards, trackers, automation, or process redesign; define clear requirements and partner with development resources on delivery. Adoption & impact tracking: Establish baselines, track adoption and action closure, and measure before/after business impact so improvements stick and benefits are evidenced. Reporting & decision support: Translate analysis into concise, decision-ready narratives and flags for account reviews and for the Assistant Manager / Manager, Business Insights.

Local teams are supported by two cross\-market teams – the Centre of Excellence, and Risk \& Control Management.
   

  

 The ICS Control Management Risk ID, Assessment, Testing \& Reporting team is responsible for identifying, assessing, mitigating, and reporting Operational Risk across ICS business processes, supporting adherence to regulatory requirements and Amex policies while strengthening the control environment and business resilience.
   

  

**Responsibilities**
 The role will be responsible for strengthening the First Line Risk \& Control framework through Process Confirmation, RCSA \& Control Development, Access Governance, Change Management, and Audit/Regulatory Support.
   

  

 The individual will partner with business teams, process owners, Legal Entity Governance, Technology, Operational Risk Management, Compliance, and other control functions to ensure risks are appropriately identified, controls remain current and effective, access risks are appropriately managed, and regulatory obligations are met.
   

  

**Key Responsibilities**
* Manage and support the transition of the existing PRSA program to RCSA, ensuring adherence to RCSA and Internal Control Framework requirements.
* Participate in RCSA activities to identify and assess inherent and residual risks, evaluate controls, identify control gaps, and develop appropriate mitigation plans.
* Partner with process owners to identify key operational and compliance risks, provide risk\-based consultation, and strengthen the overall control environment.
* Support development and maintenance of Risk \& Control Matrices (RCMs), process flowcharts, risk and control inventories, and controls documentation.
* Design and create new controls and enhance existing controls arising from RCSA findings, NPAs, OREs, Audit MAPs, regulatory requirements, and business/process changes.
* Support Change Management activities by assessing risk and control impacts arising from changes to products, processes, systems, and technology.
* Support Regulatory Obligation Management, including mapping applicable requirements to business processes and controls and identifying potential gaps.

 Risk Management team at EY plays an important role in managing the internal risks of the firm associated with accepting a new client or an engagement or risks associated with any of our on\-going audit / non audit engagement. Formed in the Year 2007, the Risk Management team is growing rapidly as a Center of Excellence for all standardized quality / compliance related activities that can be efficiently undertaken from Global Delivery Services location.

This position is designed for an experienced professional who likes to be challenged and wants to grow in a dynamic, multi\-cultural environment working with modern tools.
   

  

**Your Key Responsibilities**
 The role of a Data Analyst, in the Global Risk Management function, will have the opportunity to collaborate with teams across the globe and with internal stakeholders, which may require adjusting shift timings to manage calls and tasks effectively. It will directly impact multiple KPIs within Risk Management and drive and support key initiatives. This role will analyse data to optimize existing processes and develop new solutions. description:
Gurgaon, Haryana, India
   

  

 AXA XL is the Property \& Casualty risk division of AXA, created from the acquisition of XL Catlin in 2018\. We partner with mid\-sized to multinational clients to take their business further, with more than 30 lines of business to offer solutions for existing and emerging risks. With 9,000\+ colleagues based in approximately 30 countries we can serve clients in more than 200 countries\*.
   

  

 The Risk Analyst role supports the Credit and Country Risk Management Team, which is part of the CRO Americas, Underwriting Risk, Credit and country Risk. This role reports to the Head of Credit and Country Risk Management.
   

  

 The position requires a skilled and proactive Risk Data \& Analytics Specialist to support our credit and country risk management functions. The ideal candidate will be responsible for data management, automation initiatives, risk analysis, and reporting processes that enhance organizational risk oversight and decision\-making. This role requires effective technical expertise, innovative thinking, and the ability to collaborate across teams to improve efficiency and data integrity.
   

  

**What You’ll Be DOING**
 What will your essential responsibilities include?
   

  

* Conduct credit and country risk data aggregations using Structed Query Language (SQL) to facilitate robust risk assessment processes.
* Develop, maintain, and enhance comprehensive dashboards in Microsoft Power Business Intelligence (PBI) to enable effective risk monitoring and reporting.
* Collaborate with the business units to ensure timely, accurate, and standardized data uploads via SharePoint.
* Maintain detailed, up\-to\-date documentation of risk management procedures to ensure compliance and operational excellence.
* Support the Short\-Term Economic Capital (STEC) data requirements, ensuring accuracy and consistency.
* Utilize AI\-driven data management and analytics techniques to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of Credit and Country risk assessments.
* Automate the Ultimate Parent mapping process by exploring and integrating various tools and Application Programming Interface (APIs) to improve precision and reduce manual effort.
* Support the development and maintenance of a centralized referral management system via SharePoint, streamlining communication and automating workflow processes with business units.
* Contribute to the implementation of strategies aimed at improving consistency and efficiency in risk aggregations, ratings, sector classifications, and country data across AXA XL.
* Create and maintain educational videos to promote best practices and facilitate knowledge sharing.
* Assist in validating and assessing the suitability of credit risk tools, and models, ensuring alignment with organizational requirements and exploring alternative solutions.
* Assist in the development and refinement of risk management policies and risk tolerance frameworks.
* Support the creation and maintenance of downside scenarios, Potential Maximum Loss (PML), and Loss Given Default (LGD) metrics.
* Conduct periodic and ad hoc research on selected underwriting portfolios to inform risk assessment.
* Perform targeted, real\-time research on emerging events to support proactive risk management.
* Provide risk analysis support for complex transaction deals referred for review.
* Contribute to the updates of dashboards for risk management committees.
* Support climate risk analysis, geopolitical scenarios risk data summarization, audit, regulatory reporting, and other deliverables.
* Assist the Credit and Country Risk team with special projects and ad hoc tasks as required.


 You will report to Head of Credit and Country Risk Management.
   

  

**What You Will BRING**
 We’re looking for someone who has these abilities and skills:
   

  

**Required Skills And Abilities**
* Proven experience in risk data management, analytics, or related fields.
* Outstanding proficiency in SQL, PBI, and automation tools/APIs.
* Hands\-on experience with risk assessment, scenario analysis, and regulatory reporting requirements.
* Ability to work self\-supportedly, prioritize tasks effectively, and adapt in a dynamic environment.
* Knowledge of (re)insurance product lines and investment risk management.
* Demonstrated ability to collaborate across complex, matrix organizations to develop solutions.
* Commitment to continuous improvement with a proactive approach to streamlining processes.
* Excellent critical thinking, analytical skills, attention to detail, and a proactive mindset.
* Ability to question the status quo to constructively drive positive change.


**Desired Skills And Abilities**
* Knowledge of credit and country risk practices within the financial services or the (re)insurance industry.
* Familiarity with AI and machine learning applications in data analysis and risk modeling.
* Experience in developing and implementing risk management policies and frameworks.
* Bachelor’s and/or master’s degree in finance, Investments, Risk Management, Mathematics, or Economics.
* CFA or FRM designation is preferred.
* Relevant years of experience working within a (re)insurance company.
* Familiarity with capital modeling and/or model validation processes.


**Who WE are**
 AXA XL, the P\&C and specialty risk division of AXA, is known for solving complex risks. For mid\-sized companies, multinationals and even some inspirational individuals we don’t just provide re/insurance, we reinvent it.
   

  

 How? By combining a comprehensive and efficient capital platform, data\-driven insights, leading technology, and the best talent in an agile and inclusive workspace, empowered to deliver top client service across all our lines of business − property, casualty, professional, financial lines and specialty.
   

  

 With an innovative and flexible approach to risk solutions, we partner with those who move the world forward.
   

  

 Learn more at axaxl.com
   

  

**What we OFFER**
**Inclusion**
 AXA XL is committed to equal employment opportunity and will consider applicants regardless of gender, sexual orientation, age, ethnicity and origins, marital status, religion, disability, or any other protected characteristic. At AXA XL, we know that an inclusive culture and enables business growth and is critical to our success. That’s why we have made a strategic commitment to attract, develop, advance and retain the most inclusive workforce possible, and create a culture where everyone can bring their full selves to work and reach their highest potential.
 *It’s about helping one another — and our business — to move forward and succeed.*
* Five Business Resource Groups focused on gender, LGBTQ\+, ethnicity and origins, disability and inclusion with 20 Chapters around the globe.
* Robust support for Flexible Working Arrangements
* Enhanced family\-friendly leave benefits
* Named to the Diversity Best Practices Index
* Signatory to the UK Women in Finance Charter


 Learn more at axaxl.com/about\-us/inclusion\-and\-diversity. AXA XL is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
   

  

**Total Rewards**
 AXA XL’s Reward program is designed to take care of what matters most to you, covering the full picture of your health, wellbeing, lifestyle and financial security. It provides competitive compensation and personalized, inclusive benefits that evolve as you do.
   

  

 We’re committed to rewarding your contribution for the long term, so you can be your best self today and look forward to the future with confidence.
   

  

**Sustainability**
 At AXA XL, Sustainability is integral to our business strategy. In an ever\-changing world, AXA XL protects what matters most for our clients and communities. We know that sustainability is at the root of a more resilient future. Our 2023\-26 Sustainability strategy, called “Roots of resilience”, focuses on protecting natural ecosystems, addressing climate change, and embedding sustainable practices across our operations.
   

  

**Our Pillars**
* Valuing nature: How we impact nature affects how nature impacts us. Resilient ecosystems \- the foundation of a sustainable planet and society – are essential to our future. We’re committed to protecting and restoring nature – from mangrove forests to the bees in our backyard – by increasing biodiversity awareness and inspiring clients and colleagues to put nature at the heart of their plans.
* Addressing climate change: The effects of a changing climate are far\-reaching and significant. Unpredictable weather, increasing temperatures, and rising sea levels cause both social inequalities and environmental disruption. We're building a net zero strategy, developing insurance products and services, and mobilizing to advance thought leadership and investment in societal\-led solutions.
* Integrating ESG: All companies have a role to play in building a more resilient future. Incorporating ESG considerations into our internal processes and practices builds resilience from the roots of our business. We’re training our colleagues, engaging our external partners, and evolving our sustainability governance and reporting.
* AXA Hearts in Action: We have established volunteering and charitable giving programs to help colleagues support causes that matter most to them, known as AXA XL’s “Hearts in Action” programs. These include our Matching Gifts program, Volunteering Leave, and our annual volunteering day – the Global Day of Giving.


 For more information, please see axaxl.com/sustainability.

title: RBI Data Analysis
description:
Job Summary Credit Risk in Indian Banking: RBI Data Analysis For most of the last decade, credit risk in Indian banking meant a crisis story. Ballooning bad loans. Undercapitalised public sector banks. A system searching for a floor. That story has changed. This analysis of Indian banking credit risk data draws straight from RBI s own numbers. It shows a sector operating at some of the lowest stressed-asset levels in its history. At the same time, new risks are quietly building underneath: unsecured retail credit, gold loans, and a fast-growing NBFC sector. So for anyone building credit risk models on Indian data, the headline ratio matters less than the underlying trend. What matters is understanding where the improvement came from, and where the residual risk now sits. This piece works through what RBI s own publications actually show. Specifically, we draw on RBI s Financial Stability Report (FSR) and its Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India. We also use RBI s supervisory data releases directly. First, we break the picture down by bank category. Then we connect it to how analysts actually model default risk in practice. What Indian Banking Credit Risk Data Shows About Asset Quality How far asset quality has improved The single most-cited number here is the Gross Non-Performing Asset (GNPA) ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs). RBI s Financial Stability Report was released in June 2026. It put the GNPA ratio of SCBs at 1.8% as of March 2026 a multi-decadal low. RBI s own baseline projection expects only a slight edge-up, to around 1.9% by March 2028. The central bank called this a modest, manageable increase, not a reversal of the underlying trend. That figure looks even more striking against where the system stood less than a decade ago. In 2018, RBI s Financial Stability Report flagged a system-wide GNPA ratio of 11.46%. Banks under Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) RBI s restrictive framework for weak lenders ran even higher. The distance between 11.46% in 2018 and 1.8% in 2026 is the real story here. In fact, it represents one of the fastest deleveraging cycles any major banking system has gone through. And it wasn t accidental. It followed a specific, traceable sequence of interventions. Any credit risk analyst working with this data should be able to name them. Capital buffers moved in the same direction. RBI s June 2026 FSR put the system-wide Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) at 17.7%. The Common Equity Tier-1 (CET1) ratio stood at 15.3%. Both are multi-decade highs, per RBI. Similarly, RBI s Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India 2024-25 shows the same trend over a longer horizon. System CRAR rose from 12.94% in March 2015 to roughly 17.4% by end-March 2025. Profitability tracked the same arc. Scheduled commercial banks aggregate net profit rose too from 2.63 lakh crore in FY2022-23 to 4.01 lakh crore in FY2024-25, per RBI s Trend and Progress data. What stress tests add to the Indian banking credit risk picture RBI s stress testing adds another layer here, separate from the point-in-time ratios above. Under RBI s macro stress test scenarios in the June 2026 FSR, the banking system absorbed hypothetical adverse shocks. Even so, aggregate capital ratios stayed comfortably above regulatory minimums. Compare that to RBI s own 2018 FSR. That report projected a comparable stress scenario could push GNPA at PCA banks as high as 22.3%. It also warned that at least six banks faced a capital shortfall. The gap between those two outcomes, eight years apart, is telling. It may say more about systemic resilience than either year s baseline GNPA ratio alone. None of this means credit risk has disappeared, however. RBI s June 2026 FSR was explicit on this point: new vulnerabilities are building even as legacy NPAs shrink. Specifically, RBI surveyed banks and NBFCs for the report. They flagged rising household debt, rapid growth in gold loans, and AI-enabled cyber threats as their top risks. In other words, the credit risk profile of Indian banking hasn t shrunk so much as shifted. It has moved from the corporate and industrial exposures that dominated the 2PHONE_NUMBER cycle, toward retail and unsecured lending instead. Indian Banking Credit Risk Data by Bank Category and Sector PSBs, private banks, and foreign banks compared Aggregate numbers hide where the improvement actually concentrated, though. RBI supervisory data as of breaks the 2.15% domestic GNPA ratio down by bank category. The Ministry of Finance cited this data in a Parliament reply. Public Sector Banks (PSBs) stood at 2.50%. Private Sector Banks (PVBs) stood at 1.73%. Foreign Banks stood at just 0.80%. Interestingly, the same data shows PSBs improving faster than private or foreign banks since March 2018. In other words, the segment that was historically the weakest link has also recovered the fastest. Even so, it still carries the highest absolute ratio of the three. That PSB recovery shows up in profitability too, per RBI s Trend and Progress report. PSBs aggregate net profit rose from 1.05 lakh crore in FY2022-23 to 1.78 lakh crore in FY2024-25. That s a faster proportional gain than the system as a whole. It s consistent with a segment recovering from a lower base. Where credit concentrates: NBFCs, MSMEs, and smaller lenders Beyond the bank-vs-bank split, this Indian banking credit risk data also shows where credit itself concentrates. NBFC credit is now systemically significant. It reached 14.6% of GDP in FY25, up from 13.5% a year earlier. Industry and retail exposures made up a combined 81.1% share of that NBFC credit as of end-March 2025. Services accounted for the remaining 15.4%. On the bank side, credit to MSMEs grew faster than credit to large enterprises over the same period. Meanwhile, Small Finance Banks (SFBs) posted strong balance-sheet growth. Even so, their asset quality worsened year-on-year, even as their credit-deposit ratio improved to 86.4%. That divergence is telling: large banks and PSBs improving, SFBs under pressure. It s exactly the kind of segment-level signal a system-wide GNPA number alone won t surface. Smaller institutions tell a related story, too. The number of Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs) fell by 15 during FY25, to 1,457, as consolidation continued in that segment. Still, UCB credit growth accelerated to 6.7% the fastest pace in six years. Fraud data adds a further wrinkle here. Private sector banks accounted for 59.3% of reported fraud cases by number in FY25. Public sector banks, meanwhile, accounted for 70.7% of the total value involved. Clearly, operational risk and credit risk don t always concentrate in the same segments. How This Credit Risk Data Connects to PD Estimation A GNPA ratio is a lagging, backward-looking measure. It tells you what has already defaulted, not what s likely to default next. That s the gap probability of default (PD) modelling closes. It s also why this Indian banking credit risk data is a genuinely useful input for PD work. It s not just a macro backdrop to quote in an introduction. Two things from the data above feed directly into PD modelling in practice. First, the bank-category breakdown (PSB 2.50% vs PVB 1.73% vs Foreign 0.80%) is a natural segmentation variable. Pooling all SCBs into a single PD model would blur real structural differences in underwriting standards and portfolio.
